threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will come on time because of that silly timetable. Welcome to the real world, mate—it's more of a guideline.
Caught a whiff of plantain being cooked on the 3 bus last night—made the long wait feel like a home-cooked dinner in the middle of Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a toddler in a dinosaur costume playing in front of a kebab shop on a Saturday afternoon. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find techno parties in abandoned buildings next to grandma's fruit stand. It's a wild mash-up of old and new.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their indifference to the BART delays; they know it’s just Tuesday and have already planned around it.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo eating a burrito on the 22 Fillmore. Only in SF do fancy and casual collide like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the hidden squares where locals sip on vermut and talk about football like it’s life or death.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their over-enthusiastic attempts to try every tapas bar on the block in one weekend. Locals know it’s a marathon, not a sprint.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused at bus stops, checking your phone for the TfL app like it’s your lifeline. Locals just know when to hop on.
Last night on the 196, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with a bagpipe. Half the passengers were bemused, the other half filmed it. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I walked past the kiez and saw a group of kids setting up a makeshift outdoor cinema in the park, complete with blankets and popcorn.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can grab a currywurst from a street stand while checking out art galleries. It's like street food meets culture, all in one block.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they can spot the BART delays before they hit the news—every Friday, the same train jam in the Tube.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy calmly juggling on the bus while a toddler tried to eat his shoelaces. Classic Muni chaos, but somehow everyone was just rolling with it.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí and tapas, but it's the local bakeries on Carrer de Joan Blanques that serve the best morning croissants.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they hesitate at pedestrian crossings, waiting for non-existent traffic lights.
